newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: PRESS DIGEST - New Zealand newspapers - Oct 22.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - New Zealand newspapers - Oct 22.

text.p: Unionists are prepared to soften their stance over the Employment Contracts Act if that is the price of a Labour-led coalition with NZ First. National Distribution Union national secretary Mike Jackson made a post-election prediction on Monday that the act would not be repealed. He said amendment would be the best that could be expected. Page 1.

National and NZ First emerged from their first formal post-election talks on Monday saying only they had agreed to meet again. Neither side would comment on the meeting before or afterward, except for NZ First leader Winston Peters saying it would be about "matters of process". The parties are due to meet again at 2 p.m. on Wednesday. NZ First meets Labour at 10 a.m. the same day. Page 1.

Alliance leader Jim Anderton has made a stinging attack on former NZ First strategist Michael Laws, criticising him for "publically meddling" in coalition negotiations. Anderton is furious at Laws' citing the Alliance as a serious stumbling block to a NZ First coalition with Labour. Anderton warned NZ First leader Winston Peters the voters would by "very unforgiving" if he heeded Laws' comments and supported a National government. Page 2.
A decision on whether New Zealand would buy two more Anzac frigates was not needed until next year, Defence Minister Paul East said on Monday. Page 2.

Air New Zealand expects earnings for the 1997 year to be lower than last year's $225 million, assuming difficult trading conditions continue. The company said in its prospectus for the offer of 121 million renounceable shares that trading for July and August had been in keeping with last year's second-half performance. Page 14.

A significant fall in short-term interest rates was only weeks away as the Reserve Bank's tough stance gives way before the "inevitable", merchant banker Bancorp said on Monday. An easing in rates sanctioned by the bank could be timed around the issuing of employment statistics on November 8, Bancorp said. Page 14.

Superannuation fund managers shifted more of their investments out of New Zealand and away from shares into bonds and cash in the year ended September 30, according to a survey by Jacques Martin Hewitt. Page 14.
The New Zealand dollar hit an eight-year high on Monday, prompting exporters to warn of job losses and more companies fleeing overseas. Page 14.
Hutt Valley and Kapiti pay-TV operator Saturn Communications would consider a legal challenge to any entry by Independent Newspapers into Sky TV, Saturn chief executive Jack Matthews said. Page 14.

New Zealand First wants a signed confidentiality agreement from both National and Labour before it knuckles down to serious coalition talks with them this week. And it is likely National will agree to a request for briefings from key Government ministries such as education and health during the talks, following Treasury and Reserve Bank briefings last week.

The careers of at least nine politicians are on the line when the deadline for returning officers to receive special votes closes at 7 p.m. tonight. At least six Labour, one National and two New Zealand First candidates could be tipped out or ushered into Parliament when the final results are declared, probably tomorrow.
A Labour-New Zealand First government could rely upon Alliance support except if it risked an economic crisis, Alliance leader Jim Anderton said on Monday.
Prominent Auckland barrister and New Zealand First supporter Peter Williams QC says voters who backed Winston Peters would feel betrayed if he goes into coalition with National.

Economic policymakers risk widespread damage to the export sector if they do not change their single-minded focus on inflation, BHP New Zealand Steel managing director Malcolm Burns warned on Monday. Burns said exporters could not possibly keep pace with a New Zealand dollar rising at seven percent a year.

Power New Zealand's main council shareholders are set to spurn a $104 million offer from Mercury Energy in favour of the promise of one from Utilicorp worth nearly $30 million less. Mercury needs to prise a seven percent block free from the Utilicorp-led defenders camp if it is to win its two-year-old takeover bid for its neighbour.
Nuplex is to distribute more than $11.5 million in imputation credits to shareholders through a one-for-one taxable bonus issue of ordinary shares.
